title: Block: Tree Recursion
oneLiner: Return the height of a binary tree: the number of nodes on its longest root-to-leaf path.
keyTakeaway: Tree recursion is three lines: the base case for null, recurse into both children, combine. Write the null case first and the rest follows.
explanation:
Return the number of nodes on the longest path from the root down to a leaf. An empty tree has height 0 and a single node has height 1. Trees are given as LeetCode-style level-order lists, with null for a missing child.

If the node is null, return 0. Otherwise ask for the height of the left subtree and of the right subtree, and return 1 plus the larger. Diameter, balanced-tree checks and path sums are all this shape with a different combine step.

pythonHarnessPreamble:
null = None

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val):
        self.val = val
        self.left = None
        self.right = None

def build_level_order_tree(values):
    if not values or values[0] is None:
        return None
    root = TreeNode(values[0])
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(values):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if values[i] is not None:
            node.left = TreeNode(values[i])
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(values) and values[i] is not None:
            node.right = TreeNode(values[i])
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root
gotchas: Forgetting the null base case, or returning 1 for null, which makes every height one too big.

complexity.note: Every node is visited once; the call stack is as deep as the tree, O(h), which is O(n) for a tree shaped like a list.
